graph.name: Depop Data Architecture and Recommendation Engine
graph.notes: Architecture diagram detailing Depop's event-driven data ingestion pipeline and product recommendation engine leveraging AWS Kinesis, Lambda, Glue, S3, Athena, and EMR.

nodes.name: Kinesis
nodes.notes: Ingestion stream receiving all system events (creates, updates, deletes) from Depop services.

nodes.name: Lambda
nodes.notes: In-house fan-out Lambda function optimized to handle hundreds of thousands of peak invocations.

nodes.name: Multiple Kinesis Streams
nodes.notes: Topic-separated streams used to categorize event data for downstream Glue processing.

nodes.name: S3
nodes.notes: Stores both raw JSON event data and processed Parquet data in S3 buckets under distinct key spaces.

nodes.name: Glue
nodes.notes: Runs ETL jobs to perform data normalization, resolve type mismatches, and convert JSON to Parquet format.

nodes.name: Athena
nodes.notes: Executes SQL queries on Parquet data in S3 to prepare datasets for the recommendation engine.

nodes.name: Lambda (Scheduler)
nodes.notes: Schedules and orchestrates the recommendation pipeline every 4 to 5 hours.

nodes.name: EMR
nodes.notes: Spins up EMR cluster post-query completion to calculate product/user rankings and scores.

edges.notes: Services send user actions and system events into the primary Kinesis stream.
Fan-out Lambda fans out incoming events into distinct topic-based Kinesis streams.
Topic streams write raw JSON data to S3 under specific key paths.
Glue ETL jobs read raw JSON, normalize schema, and write Athena-optimized Parquet data back to S3.
Lambda scheduler triggers Athena SQL query execution on a schedule.
Athena queries normalized Parquet datasets stored in S3.
Athena query completion triggers the spin-up of an EMR cluster to perform scoring algorithms.
